newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher ahead of futures expiry.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher ahead of futures expiry.

text.p: French shares closed with a surprise run up on Thursday, as the market squeezed higher ahead of the expiry of November futures and options contracts.

Traders said the cash market, which had been looking to consolidate, was essentially pulled by the futures pit. Although U.S. markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday, there was good support from a strong dollar which helps U.S. funds.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended up 19.54 points or 0.86 percent at 2,290.31, just shy of key resistance around 2,300. The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,293 from 2,274 on Wednesday's close. Volume was 5.3 billion francs.
* Air Liquide ends up 2.64 percent at 817 francs after brokerages Dupont-Denant and SGE Delahaye upgraded the stock and raised profit forecasts on Wednesday.
The stock also attracted buying as investors are looking for shares which have underperformed the market.

* Compagnie Bancaire rose 4.21 percent to 594 francs, on the back of a bonus one-for-one share issue by its Cetelem unit. Cetelem, which is paying a 10 franc per share dividend on the enlarged capital, firmed 1.54 percent to 1,256.
* Havas was the biggest riser on the CAC index. La Tribune reported Alcatel Alsthom chairman has asked Havas's Pierre Dauzier actively to pursue asset values.
* Rhone-Poulenc firms 1.42 percent to 164.70. Morgan Stanley reiterates outperform recommendation as part of a revaluation of the pharmaceuticals actities of Euroepan companies.
The U.S brokerage reckons Rhone should be trading at 10 times estimated 1997 net earnings whereas it currently trades at 8.4 times, excluding Rorer.
It sees a target of 183 francs for Rhone shares.
* Eurotunnel continues correction started yesterday, closes up 4.26 percent at 7.35 francs.
The planned pooling of Channel ferry capacity by P&O and Stena has been referred to the British Monopolies and Mergers Commission, delaying the move for three months.
* Valeo ends up 2.7 percent at 319 francs. A block trade of 210,500 shares went through at 309 francs per share.
